anzsic_codes.name: Computer System Design and Related Services

merger_description:
Salesforce, Inc. (**Salesforce**) proposes to acquire 100% of the shares in Contentful Global, Inc. (**Contentful**).

Salesforce is a global supplier of customer relationship management (**CRM**) software and other software-as-a-service solutions that enable companies to manage their relationships with customers. Salesforce’s CRM platform assists users with sales, service, marketing and commerce functions.

Contentful is a global supplier of digital experience software, specifically, a content management system. Contentful’s content management system is used by businesses to create, edit, organise and publish a company's digital content across various channels and platforms via Application Programming Interfaces (**API**). Contentful provides a 'headless' content management system, meaning it stores and manages an organisation's content separately from the system that displays the content to the end user.

events.title: Salesforce - Contentful - Phase 1 determination
events.determination_commission_division: Determination made by a division of the Commission constituted by a direction issued pursuant to section 19 of the Act

determination_table_content.details:
Salesforce, Inc. (Salesforce)’s proposed acquisition of 100% of the
shares in Contentful Global, Inc. (Contentful) (the Acquisition).

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission has
determined under section 51ABZE(1) of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) that the Acquisition may be put into effect.

The acquirer, Salesforce, is a global supplier of customer
relationship management (CRM) software and other software-as-a-
service solutions. Salesforce’s modular CRM platform assists users
with sales, service, marketing and commerce functions.
The target, Contentful, is a global supplier of digital experience
software, specifically, a content management system. Contentful’s
content management system is used by businesses to create, edit,
organise and publish a company's digital content across various
channels and platforms via Application Programming Interfaces
(API). Contentful provides a 'headless' content management
product, meaning it stores and manages an organisation's content
separately from the system that displays the content to the end
user.

determination_table_content.item:
Overlap and relationship
between the Parties
determination_table_content.details:
The Parties overlap in the supply of content management system
software. Salesforce also offers products that can interoperate with
Contentful’s content management system.

When making a determination in Phase 1, the Australian Competition
and Consumer Commission (ACCC) undertakes a competition
assessment and considers whether it is appropriate for an
acquisition to be approved or subject to further assessment in
Phase 2 in accordance with section 51ABZJ of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act). In doing so, the ACCC must have
regard to the object of the Act and all relevant matters, including the
interests of consumers.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notified acquisitions, see the ACCC’s merger assessment guidelines
and interim merger process guidelines.
In conducting its competition assessment, the ACCC has considered
the information and documents that were submitted with the
notification form and feedback from third parties.
The ACCC has determined that the Acquisition may be put into
effect as it considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to have the
effect of substantially lessening competition in any market. In
reaching its decision, and based on the material before it, the ACCC
makes the following findings.
• There is minimal horizontal overlap between Salesforce and
Contentful in the supply of content management systems.
Salesforce’s current content management software is not
offered as a standalone product and is limited in its capabilities
compared to those of Contentful as well as other content
management systems and digital experience platforms.
• Post-acquisition, the merged firm would continue to face
competition from alternative suppliers of content management
systems, including Acquia, Adobe, Contently, Optimizely and
Sanity.
• The merged firm would be unlikely to have the ability and
incentive to foreclose rival providers of content management
systems via an anti-competitive bundling or tying strategy given
there are alternative suppliers of CRM services in Australia and
internationally. Market feedback also indicates that the merged
firm would continue to have the incentive to maintain
interoperability between its software and rivals’ products.

A notifying party, or other person who has been allowed to do so by
the Australian Competition Tribunal, may apply for review if they are
dissatisfied with the determination. Pursuant to section 100C of the
Act, applications for review of the determination are to be made to
the Australian Competition Tribunal before the end of 14 calendar
days after this statement of reasons was included on the ACCC’s
Acquisitions Register. To confirm whether there has been any
application for review, please contact the Australian Competition
Tribunal.
